text: According to the lab materials, why is NARMA-10 considered a demanding benchmark?
choices: It has a chaotic attractor that is impossible to predict beyond a few steps
It requires both roughly 10 steps of memory and a nonlinear interaction of past values
Its input is high-dimensional, forcing the use of a very large reservoir
Its targets are discrete symbols that must be classified exactly
explanation: The target depends on the full past 10 steps (memory) and on nonlinear products (0.05·y·Σ and 1.5·u·u), so a model must supply both memory AND nonlinearity. NARMA-10 is not chaotic (that is Mackey-Glass/Lorenz), its input is scalar, and its targets are continuous values.
